phase_name: Authority Evaluation Model Implementation Contract Repair
summary: Phase 147E.1 repaired Finding BF-147F-1 (Phase 147F, Blocking) in AEMIC-001: v1.0's evaluate() function was frozen with a closed, exactly-four-parameter signature (claimed_identity, declaration, evaluated_at, evaluator_version) and EligibleAuthorityDeclaration was frozen to exactly six fields, neither carrying citation_text, yet AEMIC-REQ-022 required every eligible-result AuthorityEvaluationOutcome to carry a non-None citation_text enforced at construction time with evaluate() as the contract's sole specified construction path; v1.0 AEMIC-REQ-031's own text was internally self-contradictory on this exact point. This phase independently re-derived the contradiction directly from AEMIC-001 v1.0's own text before consulting Phase 147F's report a second time for comparison, confirmed every affected requirement, and evaluated three candidate repairs: widening EligibleAuthorityDeclaration (rejected as foreclosed by AEM-001's own AEM-REQ-007 closed six-field freeze -- not merely architecturally inferior, since AEMIC-001 itself forbids narrowing or amending AEM-001), adding a citation_text channel to evaluate() (selected), and a distinct bypass-evaluate() construction path (rejected as fragmenting the single-enforcement-point discipline for no benefit). AEMIC-001 is now v1.1: citation_text: str | None = None is evaluate()'s own fifth parameter (Sec.5, AEMIC-REQ-019), enforced by new AEMIC-REQ-101 (Sec.14.1) which raises a new exception, MissingCitationTextError, when the internally-determined evaluation_result is ELIGIBLE and no citation was supplied, and disregards (never raises on, never fabricates from) a citation supplied alongside an INELIGIBLE or INDETERMINATE result. Sections 5, 9, 13.1, 14, 15, 20, 22, and 23 were amended; every other section is byte-for-byte unchanged from v1.0; no AEMIC-REQ-### identifier was renumbered, retired, or reused; two new identifiers were appended (AEMIC-REQ-101, AEMIC-REQ-102). BF-147F-1 is marked Repaired in Sec.23's Finding Disposition table; F-147F-2 (Unicode normalization) and F-147F-3 (forbidden-import test not yet extended) remain open, Non-Blocking, and explicitly outside this repair's own scope. Security review confirmed caller-controlled citation fabrication risk is unchanged relative to v1.0's own intended design, not newly introduced or worsened. Compatibility review confirmed zero schema, runtime, IWC-001, or PEC-001 change, and confirmed AEM-001 and Phase 147D's own architecture are both preserved except for the one gap Phase 147D's Sec.6.2 itself left open. Overall Verdict: IMPLEMENTATION CONTRACT REPAIRED. Full detail in docs/PHASE_147E.1_AUTHORITY_EVALUATION_MODEL_IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACT_REPAIR.md.
